== Proposed new article: Reflective higher-order calculus (COI disclosure) ==

{{connected contributor|User=YOUR_USERNAME|declared=yes}}

'''Conflict of interest disclosure.''' I am one of the two authors of the 2005 paper that introduced the reflective higher-order calculus, and I am an officer of F1R3FLY.io, which maintains one of the implementations mentioned in the draft. Per [[WP:COI]] I am not editing the article directly. I am posting a draft here and asking uninvolved editors to review it, cut what does not belong, and move any part they judge suitable into article space. I will not restore material that a reviewer removes.

'''What I am proposing.''' This page currently distinguishes two unrelated calculi that share the name "rho calculus": the rewriting calculus of Cirstea and Kirchner, and the reflective higher-order calculus of Meredith and Radestock. Only the second has any content here, and only one sentence of it.

I would suggest, rather than expanding this page, that:

# a standalone article be created at '''[[Reflective higher-order calculus]]''', using the draft below or whatever survives review of it;
# this page be reworked as a proper disambiguation page pointing to that article and to a treatment of the rewriting calculus.

I have no view on the naming and defer entirely to editors here. I would note only that the literature is split: the introducing paper and most subsequent work write "ρ-calculus", while "rho calculus" and "RHO calculus" are also common, so redirects from all three forms seem worth having whatever title is chosen.

'''On sourcing.''' The draft leans on independent secondary sources wherever it can, principally Stian Lybech's work at Reykjavík University and the group at Aalborg — an ''Information and Computation'' article devoted to the calculus (2024), an EXPRESS/SOS paper (2022), the higher-order Ψ-calculi type-system papers, and the AGERE paper on the localised variant. Several of these correct or contradict the original paper, and I have kept those corrections in the draft rather than softening them; the 2022 paper identifies two errors in my own encoding of the π-calculus, and the draft says so.

Three places where I would particularly welcome scrutiny:

* The '''implementations''' section cites GitHub repositories, which are primary and self-published, and one of them is my company's. I have tagged it. If reviewers think the whole section fails [[WP:PROMO]] or [[WP:PRIMARY]], removing it would not trouble me.
* Two subsections under '''Variations''' are deliberately incomplete, marked with HTML comments, because I could not find published sources for them. They should be either sourced or dropped before the article goes live.
* The '''namespace logic''' and '''categorical semantics''' sections rest largely on papers I co-authored. They are peer-reviewed or preprints of record, but they are not independent, and a reviewer may reasonably want them trimmed to what secondary sources support.

Draft follows in the subpage linked below. Comments and cuts welcome.
